Subject: Re: Model governance questionnaire — completed answers (inline)

Alan / Globex team —

Replying inline to the governance topics you called out (pulled from the questionnaire). For readability I've grouped responses by topic.

1) Catalog & provenance- We publish a machine-readable catalog export and per-model model-card that includes: upstream license tag, training data provenance summary (high-level, not PII), model architecture, tokenizer, and a SHA256 of the published weights. The catalog export (attached manifest) also contains a timestamped lineage chain when we perform conversion/quantization steps (example: base-model -> quantized-8bit-v1). We can provide signed manifests for pre-production artifacts on request.

2) Open-model licensing and compliance- Redwood does not relicense upstream models. We ingest license metadata from upstream repos and apply permissibility rules in our catalog. For each model we surface: license name, commercial-use flag, modification flag, attribution requirements, and incompatible license warnings. Models flagged as incompatible with your policy can be filtered at the organization level. We also provide a short report format that lists any third-party license obligations you must accept when deploying a model (attachment: model_catalog_manifest.json).

3) Version pinning and runtimes- API-level pinning is first-class: clients supply model_id and model_version (semantic style e.g. 2.1.0 or snapshot id). When you pin a version we serve the exact artifact (weights hash + runtime ops) referenced in the signed manifest. We also support immutable snapshot IDs for long-term reproducibility; snapshots include the exact kernel/quantization profile used. Pinning prevents automatic rollforward for that route unless you change the configuration. For customers on Redwood Dedicated/Private we support exporting the pinned artifact for air-gapped deployment.

4) Update notifications, regressions, and opt-in rollouts- We maintain a model lifecycle topic where we publish release notes and breaking-change flags. Customers can choose: automatic safe-rollforward (minor performance/security patches only), explicit opt-in for major updates, or strict pinned mode (no automatic updates). We back these with per-model quality checks and an optional canary traffic mechanism with automatic rollback on metric regressions (latency/quality delta).

5) Evidence & auditability- We can provide: signed weight hashes (model_weights_hashes.txt), historical catalog snapshots, and a download log for any artifact retrieval. Our audit logs include model_id, version, timestamp, and the requesting tenant ID for Dedicated/Private customers. SOC 2 Type II report is attached for your compliance team to review.

6) Proprietary modifications- If Redwood or a partner produces a derivative or fine-tuned variant, we surface both the upstream provenance and a derivative manifest that documents the forked changes, training dataset summary, and license implications. Derivative models are tagged in the catalog with "derivative:true" and linked to their parent model id.

If you'd like, we can extract the subset of the answers you need into a short compliance packet (csv + signed hashes) for your vendor intake system.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Model Catalog
Redwood Inference

Attachment: model_catalog_manifest.json; model_weights_hashes.txt

Subject: Re: Model governance questionnaire — export & contract notes

Alan —

Short answers: yes on both. Operationally we produce a signed tarball of the pinned artifact (weights + manifest + runtime shim) that you can import into an air-gapped evaluation cluster; we can coordinate transfer via a presigned secure bucket or an SFTP transfer for Dedicated/Private deals.

On contract language: we typically include a clause that derivative models retain the original upstream license obligations where applicable and that Redwood will not relicense third-party-provided models. For fine-tunes built using Redwood-managed datasets or significant Redwood-owned IP, we negotiate a downstream redistribution clause per deal (we can provide a redline sample). I can have our legal team push a short MSA addendum and sample redistribution language to the drive link below.
